title: 通り and せっかく
summary: 通り is a road of agreement ("just as"), and せっかく marks something precious or gained with effort.

blocks.text: **通り** is the い-stem noun of 通る (pass through): a road, a way. **Modifier + 通り** means "following the way of ...", i.e. "just as ...".

blocks.jp: ご覧の通り、店は閉まっている。
blocks.en: As you can see, the shop is closed.

blocks.text: その通り ("that road") means "exactly right": you are thinking along the right road. After a noun it is read どおり (思い通り, 予定通り).
せっかく: precious and hard to replace

The dictionary offers many meanings (with effort, precious, especially), but all come from one idea: this thing is valuable and not easily replaced, so something should be done with it, or it is a pity it is lost.

blocks.jp: せっかく京都に来たのだから、お寺に行こう。
blocks.en: Since we've come all the way to Kyoto, let's go to a temple.

blocks.jp: せっかくの休日が雨で台無しだ。
blocks.en: My precious day off is ruined by rain.

blocks.jp: せっかく作ったのに、誰も食べない。
blocks.en: I went to the trouble of making it, but nobody eats it.

items: **Modifier + 通り** = just as ...; その通り = exactly.
**せっかく** = a rare chance or effort, so make use of it (or what a pity).

questions.instruction: What does その通り mean?
questions.note: Following the same road of thought.

questions.instruction: What does 思い通りにならない mean?
options: Things don't go as I want
questions.note: 思い = will, desire.

questions.instruction: What does せっかく emphasize?
options: Something rare, valuable, or the effort taken
questions.note: Preciousness.

questions.prompt: 通り after a noun can be read どおり.
questions.note: 予定どおり.

questions.prompt: せっかく always means "with great haste".
questions.note: It means precious or hard-won.
questions.en: A rare chance; going to the trouble.

questions.prompt: この地図の＿＿に行けば、駅に着く。
questions.note: Modifier + 通り: just as.
questions.en: If you go according to this map, you'll reach the station.

questions.prompt: 先生が言った＿＿にやってみた。
questions.note: 言った通り: just as (the teacher) said.
questions.en: I tried it just as the teacher said.

questions.prompt: ＿＿作ったのに、食べてくれなかった。
questions.note: せっかく: I went to the trouble, but it was wasted.
questions.en: I went to the trouble of making it, but he didn't eat it.

questions.instruction: What does せっかく express?
questions.prompt: せっかく晴れたのだから、洗濯しよう。
options: A rare chance should be used
questions.note: せっかく: since this is valuable, make use of it.
questions.en: Since the weather has cleared up, let's do the laundry.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "It finished exactly as planned"?
questions.note: Noun + 通り: according to.

questions.instruction: How is 通り read after a noun like 約束?
questions.note: After a noun it becomes どおり.
言った通り: just as I said.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that shows the wasted effort
questions.note: せっかく: I went to the trouble of buying it.
questions.en: I went to the trouble of buying it, and yet it broke.

questions.prompt: I went just as the map said.
questions.note: Noun の + 通りに: according to.
questions.en: I went just as the map said.

questions.prompt: Since it's a rare chance, let's eat out.
questions.note: せっかくだから: since it's a rare chance.
questions.en: Since it's a rare chance, let's eat out.

questions.prompt: I went to the trouble of coming, but the shop was closed.
questions.note: せっかく ... のに: wasted effort.
questions.en: I went to the trouble of coming, but the shop was closed.

questions.prompt: It turned out just as I thought.
questions.note: Modifier + 通りに.
questions.en: It turned out just as I thought.

questions.prompt: せっかく always shows a negative feeling.
questions.note: It can also push you to make use of a chance.
questions.en: A rare chance can be good or bad.

questions.prompt: 予定通り means "according to plan".
questions.note: Noun + どおり: according to.

questions.instruction: Which situation fits せっかく?
options: You made a big dinner, but nobody came
questions.note: A valuable effort that was wasted.

options: The い-stem noun of 通る: a way, a road
questions.note: Modifier + 通り fills the noun 通り.
